question_content: pA multi-node application runs on Amazon EC2 instances that run in several subnets within the same VPC. Instance A (172.31.16.139) initiates communication to Instance B (10.10.128.14) on port 5001. Communication between the instances is not successful. A solutions architect analyzes VPC flow logs to identify the problem and discovers the following log entries:p2 123456789010 eni-1235b8ca123456789 172.31.16.139 10.10.128.14 20641 5001 6 20 4249 1418530010 1418530070 ACCEPT OKp2 123456789010 eni-1235b8ca123456789 10.10.128.14 172.31.16.139 5001 20641 6 20 4249 1418530192 1418530265 REJECT OKpWhich solution will resolve this problem?

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify any host-based firewalls on Instance B to allow inbound communications on TCP port 20641.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. VPC flow logs represent metadata about network packets that flow through the VPC. VPC flow logs do not contain information that indicates what the operating system of an instance will accept or reject.pFor more information about VPC flow logs and what they capture, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html#flow-logs-basics"Flow Logs Basics/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the network ACL in the Instance B subnet to allow outbound communications on port 20641.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. VPC flow logs represent metadata about network packets that flow through the VPC. Network traffic appears to be allowed to exit the network interface. However, the response is not allowed. The problem must be with the network ACL because security groups are stateful and would automatically allow return traffic. Reconfiguration of the network ACL to allow traffic to return on the appropriate ports is the correct solution.pFor more information about VPC flow logs and what they capture, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html#flow-logs-basics"Flow Logs Basics/a. pFor more information about security groups and network ACL interpretation within the VPC flow logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-records-examples.html#flow-log-example-security-groups"Security Group and Network ACL Rules/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the inbound rules for the security group on eni-1235b8ca123456789 to allow port 20641.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. VPC flow logs represent metadata about network packets that flow through the VPC. Network traffic appears to be allowed to exit the network interface. However, the response is not allowed. Security groups are stateful and would automatically allow return traffic.pFor more information about VPC flow logs and what they capture, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html#flow-logs-basics"Flow Logs Basics/a. pFor more information about security groups and network ACL interpretation within the VPC Flow Logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-records-examples.html#flow-log-example-security-groups"Security Group and Network ACL Rules/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the main route table in the VPC to allow inbound and outbound traffic to both instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. VPC flow logs represent metadata about network packets that flow through the VPC. This is not a routing problem because the logs indicate that the traffic has been rejected at the network interface.pFor more information about VPC flow logs and what they capture, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html#flow-logs-basics"Flow Logs Basics/a. pFor more information about the local route, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Route_Tables.html#route-table-routes"Routes/a.

question_content: pA company has developed a single-page web application in JavaScript. The source code is stored in a single Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company serves the web application to a global user base through Amazon CloudFront.pThe company wants to experiment with two versions of the website without informing application users. Each version of the website will reside in its own S3 bucket. The company wants to determine which version is most successful in marketing a new product.pThe solution must send application users that are based in Europe to the new website design. The solution must send application users that are based in the United States to the current website design. However, some exceptions exist. The company needs to be able to redirect specific users to the new website design, regardless of the users' location.pWhich solution meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure two CloudFront distributions. Configure a geolocation routing policy in Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to the appropriate CloudFront endpoint based on the location of clients.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A geolocation policy routes traffic based on the location of client. However, the company requires some exceptions to the forwarding rules. Rule exceptions are available through Route 53.pFor more information about how to use Route 53 to route traffic based on user geographic location, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geo.html"Geolocation Routing/a. pFor more information about Route 53 routing options, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy.html"Choosing a Routing Policy/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure a single CloudFront distribution. Create a behavior with different paths for each version of the site. Configure Lambda@Edge on the default path to generate redirects and send the client to the correct version of the website.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would inform the user of the different versions by the different paths. You would associate Lambda@Edge with a CloudFront distribution, not a path.pFor more information about how to attach Lambda@Edge to a CloudFront distribution, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-edge-how-it-works.html"Get Started Creating and Using Lambda@Edge Functions/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure a single CloudFront distribution. Configure an alternate domain name on the distribution. Configure two behaviors to route users to the different S3 origins based on the domain name that the client uses in the HTTP request.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution allows users to route themselves by the HTTP request the users submit. However, the company requires a solution that routes users based on user location. The different domain names would inform the users of the two different website versions.pFor more information about how to configure CloudFront for multiple origins and behaviors, see href="https://aws.amazon.comremiumsupport/knowledge-center/cloudfront-distribution-serve-content/"Can I Use a Single CloudFront Web Distribution to Serve Content from Multiple Origins Using Multiple Behaviors?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure a single CloudFront distribution with Lambda@Edge. Use Lambda@Edge to send user requests to different origins based on request attributes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use Lambda@Edge to dynamically route users to any origin from a CloudFront distribution based on request attributes such as headers. You can use this strategy to serve different versions of pages for A/B testing.pFor more information about how to use Lambda@Edge for A/B testing, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-examples.html#lambda-examples-a-b-testing"Example: A/B Testing/a. pFor more information about how to use Lambda@Edge for custom responses based on user location, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-examples.html#lambda-examples-redirect-based-on-country"Example: Redirecting Viewer Requests to a Country-Specific URL/a. pFor more information about how to initiate a Lambda function before CloudFront forwards a request, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-at-the-edge.html"Customizing at the Edge with Lambda@Edge/a.

question_content: pA company's chief financial officer (CFO) wants advanced notification if projections show that the costs for Amazon EC2 instances will exceed 75% of the company's monthly AWS budget. To reduce costs, the CFO wants specific EC2 instances to stop when the CFO receives the advanced notification. A solutions architect plans to use an AWS Budgets alert as part of the solution.pWhich solution will meet the CFO's requirements with the LOWEST risk of future overspending?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an alert based on actual costs of 75% of the monthly budget, filtered on instance type. Add an AWS Budgets action to stop the specified EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This AWS Budgets alert would activate when the actual expenditure reaches the threshold. The requirements are based on projected spending. An alert based on actual spending would be too late.pFor more information about AWS Budgets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/budgets-managing-costs.html"Managing Your Costs with AWS Budgets/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an alert based on actual costs of 75% of the monthly budget, filtered on instance type. Send an alert to a systems operator to stop the specified EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This AWS Budgets alert would activate when the actual expenditure reaches the threshold. The requirements are based on projected spending. An alert based on actual spending would be too late.pFor more information about AWS Budgets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/budgets-managing-costs.html"Managing Your Costs with AWS Budgets/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an alert based on projected costs of 75% of the monthly budget, filtered on instance type. Add an AWS Budgets action to stop the specified EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This AWS Budgets alert would activate when the projected expenditure reaches the threshold. An automatic AWS Budgets action is the best way to stop the EC2 instances. This automatic stop would prevent future overspending.pFor more information about AWS Budgets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/budgets-managing-costs.html"Managing Your Costs with AWS Budgets/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an alert based on projected costs of 75% of the monthly budget, filtered on instance type. Send an alert to a systems operator to stop the specified EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This AWS Budgets alert could partially meet the requirements because it would activate an alert based on projected expenditure. However, the manual step that requires the systems operator to stop the specified EC2 instances could result in overspending if the systems operator does not stop the EC2 instances quickly. An automatic AWS Budgets action is the best way to stop the EC2 instances. The automatic stop would prevent future overspending.pFor more information about AWS Budgets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/budgets-managing-costs.html"Managing Your Costs with AWS Budgets/a.

question_content: pA company is developing a new game app for mobile devices. The app has two user tiers: one tier for free-play users and another tier for premium users.pThe company currently uses custom identity authentication across its apps. The company wants to continue to use custom authentication if possible. However, the company's custom identity provider (IdP) is not compatible with either the SAML or OpenID Connect (OIDC) standards. A solutions architect needs to design an authentication approach that makes it easy to transition free-play users to premium users.pWhich design will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a single Amazon Cognito identity pool. Develop an authentication provider for the pool that calls the existing custom IdP. Implement two separate authentication flows in the mobile app: one for the free-play users and one for the premium users.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The code for the authentication provider would be a wrapper that allows the company to use its existing identity authentication functionality. The company should design the mobile app with two authentication flows to support free-play users and premium users. The use of a single identity pool also supports an easy transition between the free-play tier and the premium tier.pFor more information about how to create a developer authenticated identity provider, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/developer-authenticated-identities.html"Developer Authenticated Identities (Identity Pools)/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Cognito user pool for the premium users. Add a user pool sign-in through the custom IdP. Create a second Amazon Cognito user pool to provide guest access for the free-play users.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The company has a custom IdP that is not based on SAML or OIDC. The user pool sign-in features of Amazon Cognito would not support the company's custom IdP. Significant development effort would be necessary to build a new IdP that is compliant with SAML or OIDC.pFor more information about supported IdPs for Amazon Cognito user pools, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-identity-pools.html"Amazon Cognito User Pools/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate two Amazon Cognito identity pools. Develop an authentication provider for the premium user identity pool that calls the existing custom IdP. For the second identity pool, configure an authentication flow for the free-play users.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The creation of two identity pools would potentially require double the development work. This design would also be difficult to implement on the mobile app side. The use of two pools would also make the transition between the free-play tier and the premium tier more difficult. Significant development effort would be necessary to create a new premium user in the respective identity pool and to remove the user from the free-play user identity pool.pFor more information about how to create a developer authenticated identity provider, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/developer-authenticated-identities.html"Developer Authenticated Identities (Identity Pools)/a. pFor more information about how to add users to an identity pool, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/authentication-flow.html"Identity Pools (Federated Identities) Authentication Flow/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a single Amazon Cognito user pool. Add a user pool sign-in through the custom IdP. Set up Amazon Cognito guest access in the same user pool for the free-play users.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The company has a custom IdP that is not based on SAML or OIDC. The user pool sign-in features in Amazon Cognito would not support the company's custom IdP. Significant development effort would be necessary to build a new IdP that is compliant with SAML or OIDC.pFor more information about supported IdPs for Amazon Cognito user pools, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-identity-pools.html"Amazon Cognito User Pools/a.

question_content: pA company manages 50 AWS accounts through AWS Organizations. Different workloads in these accounts require different security groups with appropriate rules. The company's security team wants to allow SSH access only from trusted IP CIDR blocks in all AWS accounts. The security team wants to ensure that this implementation remains compliant and cannot be modified by other accounts.How can a solutions architect meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a firewall policy for AWS Network Firewall in AWS Firewall Manager. Add a stateless rule group to allow SSH access from trusted IP CIDR blocks with the lowest order priority. Restrict SSH access from 0.0.0.0/0. Select all accounts for this policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A firewall policy with a stateless group will allow or restrict traffic based on the rules within the group. In a stateless group, rules are processed starting from the lowest numbered priority setting. A rule that restricts SSH access from trusted sources will be processed and allowed first. The rest of the SSH traffic (0.0.0.0/0) will be restricted. These network firewalls and rule groups cannot be modified by the member accounts of an organization on AWS Organizations. This solution fulfills all the requirements.pFor more information about Network Firewall policies in Firewall Manager, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"AWS Network Firewall Policies. pFor more information about stateless rule groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/stateless-rule-groups-5-tuple.html"Stateless Rule Groups in AWS Network Firewall/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a common security group policy in AWS Firewall Manager. Add a primary security group with an SSH rule that allows access from trusted IP CIDR blocks. Provide the option to identify resources that do not comply with the policy rules. Select all accounts for this policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Firewall Manager does not restrict SSH access from any other sources. Additionally, Firewall Manager does not automatically remediate such broad SSH access. For these reasons, this solution does not meet the requirements.pFor more information about common security group policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/security-group-policies.html#security-group-policies-common"Common Security Group Policies/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a firewall policy for AWS Network Firewall in AWS Firewall Manager. Add a stateful rule group with a strict evaluation order to allow SSH access from trusted IP CIDR blocks with the highest order priority. Restrict SSH access from 0.0.0.0/0. Select all accounts for this policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A stateful rule group with a strict evaluation order will evaluate the rules by order of priority, starting from the lowest number. In this scenario, a rule that restricts SSH access from 0.0.0.0/0 will be evaluated first and will restrict all traffic, including SSH access from the trusted sources. This solution does not meet the requirements.pFor more information about stateful rule groups with strict evaluation order, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/suricata-rule-evaluation-order.html#suricata-strict-rule-evaluation-order"Strict Evaluation Order/a. pFor more information about standard stateful rule groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/stateful-rule-groups-basic.html"Standard Stateful Rule Groups in AWS Network Firewall/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a content audit security group policy in AWS Firewall Manager. Configure custom policy rules to deny SSH traffic from 0.0.0.0/0. Use an audit security group to allow SSH traffic from trusted IP CIDR blocks. Enable automatic remediation for any noncompliant resources. Select all accounts for this policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A content audit security group policy in Firewall Manager is used to audit security groups across multiple accounts and to recognize any noncompliant rules. Policy rules can either allow or deny rules defined in the audit security group, but not both. With this setting, other security groups across accounts are evaluated. In this scenario, the policy rule allows SSH traffic from trusted IP CIDR blocks and denies SSH traffic from 0.0.0.0/0. This denial is not possible. Additionally, other security groups across accounts must be within the scope of the audit security group. Any out-of-scope rules will make these security groups noncompliant. Automatic remediation will occur, and Firewall Manager will remove any additional rules. Such actions will disrupt multiple workloads across all accounts.pFor more information about content audit security group policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/security-group-policies.html#security-group-policies-audit"Content Audit Security Group Policies/a. pFor more information about content audit security group policy remediation actions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/security-group-content-audit-policy-findings.html"Security Group Content Audit Policy Findings/a.

question_content: pA company has deployed a Python application on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The application includes a stateless frontend, an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ database, and a two-node Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to offload the database read requests for frequently accessed data.pThe number of read requests to the database is increasing. A solutions architect adds two more nodes to the ElastiCache cluster. However, performance does not appear to improve after the addition of the nodes, and the new Memcached instances seem idle.pHow can the solutions architect resolve this issue with the LEAST code changes?

answer_choices.choice_content: pReplace the ElastiCache for Memcached cluster with an ElastiCache for Redis cluster that has cluster mode disabled. Add four read replicas to the Redis cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Additional Redis replicas would likely increase the read performance of the caching solution. However, if you replace the Memcached cluster with a Redis cluster, you would have to completely reconfigure the application to use Redis APIs. This reconfiguration would involve significant code changes.pFor more information about Redis cluster read replicas, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Replication.Redis.Groups.html"Understanding Redis Replication/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS CLI to discover the newly added node endpoints. Configure the application for reads and writes to all the endpoints.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. ElastiCache for Memcached can support Auto Discovery for certain clients. Auto Discovery is not in use in this scenario because the newly added nodes are not being discovered. You need to add the new endpoints to the application code. Some code change would be necessary, but this process would not require a complete rewrite of the code that interacts with Memcached.pFor more information about how to discover connection endpoints for a newly added Memcached node, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/Endpoints.html"Finding Connection Endpoints/a. pFor more information about how to connect to cache nodes manually, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/AutoDiscovery.Manual.html"Connecting to Cache Nodes Manually/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS CLI to discover the newly added node endpoints. Configure the RDS database for reads and writes to all the endpoints.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot configure the RDS database to perform any reads and writes against the Memcached cluster. The application reads and writes to the cache.pFor more information about database caches, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/database-caching-strategies-using-redis/types-of-database-caching.html"Types of Database Caching/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pReplace the ElastiCache for Memcached cluster with an ElastiCache for Redis cluster that has cluster mode enabled. Add four shards to the Redis cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The addition of a Redis cluster with shards would likely increase the read and write performance of the caching solution. However, if you replace the Memcached cluster with a Redis cluster, you would have to completely reconfigure the application to use Redis APIs. This reconfiguration would involve significant code changes.pFor more information about how to enable Redis cluster mode and how to configure shards, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Replication.Redis-RedisCluster.html"Replication: Redis (Cluster Mode Disabled) vs. Redis (Cluster Mode Enabled)/a.

question_content: pA company uses several services to store important data within a single AWS Region. These services include Amazon S3, Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS), Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS), Amazon RDS, and on-premises storage servers. The company wants a backup and data protection solution that would offer Regional protection for all the company's existing data. The solution must automate the processes on AWS as much as possible. The company has configured AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway for the on-premises data.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure AWS DataSync to replicate the data that is in EFS file systems to another Region. Create a cross-Region backup plan in AWS Backup that includes data that is in S3 buckets, EBS volumes, RDS databases, and the Storage Gateway volumes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Backup can automatically back up data that is in S3 buckets, Storage Gateway volumes, EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and RDS databases. Replicas of the EFS file systems are not necessary and would incur unnecessary operational overhead.pFor more information about AWS Backup, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/whatisbackup.html"What Is AWS Backup?/a pFor more information about DataSync, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/what-is-datasync.html"What Is AWS DataSync?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Backup backup vault in another Region. Create a cross-Region backup plan in AWS Backup by using the vault that includes data that is in S3 buckets, EBS volumes, EFS file systems, RDS databases, and the Storage Gateway volumes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS Backup can automatically back up data that is in S3 buckets, Storage Gateway volumes, EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and RDS databases. A cross-Region backup plan would offer the required Regional protection for the data. This solution would incur the least operational overhead.pFor more information about AWS Backup, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/whatisbackup.html"What Is AWS Backup?/a pFor more information about cross-Region replication for Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html#crr-scenario"When to Use Cross-Region Replication/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a read replica of the RDS databases in another Region. Create a cross-Region backup plan in AWS Backup that includes the data that is in S3 buckets, EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and the Storage Gateway volumes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Backup can automatically back up data that is in S3 buckets, Storage Gateway volumes, EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and RDS databases. RDS read replicas are not a backup solution. Read replicas of the RDS databases would not address the requirements but would add unnecessary operational overhead.pFor more information about AWS Backup, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/whatisbackup.html"What Is AWS Backup?/a pFor more information about RDS read replicas, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html"Working with Read Replicas/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate EBS snapshots and copy the EBS snapshots to a different Region. Create a cross-Region backup plan in AWS Backup that includes data that is in S3 buckets, EFS file systems, RDS databases, and the Storage Gateway volumes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Backup can automatically back up data that is in S3 buckets, Storage Gateway volumes, EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and RDS databases. However, it is not necessary to use DataSync to replicate the EBS volumes because AWS Backup can back up EBS volumes. Cross-Region replication would automatically protect the data that is in S3 buckets with less operational overhead.pFor more information about AWS Backup, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/whatisbackup.html"What Is AWS Backup?/a pFor more information about cross-Region replication for Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html#crr-scenario"When to Use Cross-Region Replication/a. pFor more information about how to copy EBS snapshots, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-copy-snapshot.html"Copy an Amazon EBS Snapshot/a.

question_content: pA company has a website that enables users to upload videos. Company policy states the uploaded videos must be analyzed for restricted content. An uploaded video is placed in Amazon S3, and a message is pushed to an Amazon SQS queue with the video's location. A backend application pulls this location from Amazon SQS and analyzes the video.pThe video analysis is compute-intensive and occurs sporadically during the day. The website scales with demand. The video analysis application runs on a fixed number of instances. Peak demand occurs during the holidays, so the company must add instances to the application during this time. All instances used are currently on-demand Amazon EC2 T2 instances. The company wants to reduce the cost of the current solution.pWhich of the following solutions is MOST cost-effective?

answer_choices.choice_content: pKeep the website on T2 instances. Determine the minimum number of website instances required during off-peak times and use Spot Instances to cover them while using Reserved Instances to cover peak demand. Use Amazon EC2 R4 and Amazon EC2 R5 Reserved Instances in an Auto Scaling group for the video analysis application.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The memory-focused R family is not the best use case for compute-intensive video analysis. If you use Spot Instances to cover the minimum off-peak website demand, you may not achieve the total target capacity. Reserved Instances are cost-effective when there is a predictable pattern of usage. However, the video analysis task is sporadic.

answer_choices.choice_content: pKeep the website on T2 instances. Determine the minimum number of website instances required during off-peak times and use Reserved Instances to cover them while using On-Demand Instances to cover peak demand. Use Spot Fleet for the video analysis application comprised of Amazon EC2 C4 and Amazon EC2 C5 Spot Instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. It is cost-effective to use Reserved Instances to cover predictable website traffic off-peak. On-Demand instances are cost-effective for unpredictable holiday peak traffic. A fleet of Spot Instances for a sporadic video analysis application is cost-effective. C4 and C5 Spot Instances are the best fit for the video analysis application because this application is compute intensive.pFor more information about cost optimization with Spot Instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-technical-content/latest/cost-optimization-leveraging-ec2-spot-instances/when-to-use-spot-instances.html"When to Use Spot Instances/a.pFor more information about EC2 instance use cases, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/instance-types/%20"Amazon EC2 Instance Types/a.pFor  more information about how to choose the correct EC2 instance type, see href="https://aws.amazon.comremiumsupport/knowledge-center/ec2-instance-choose-type-for-workload/"How Do I Choose the Appropriate EC2 Instance Type for My Workload?/apFor more information about EC2 Reserved Instances, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/ec2ricing/reserved-instances/"Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pMigrate the website to AWS Elastic Beanstalk and Amazon EC2 C4 instances. Determine the minimum number of website instances required during off-peak times and use On-Demand Instances to cover them while using Spot capacity to cover peak demand. Use Spot Fleet for the video analysis application comprised of C4 and Amazon EC2 C5 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Compute-optimized C4 instances are not as cost-effective for web servers as T2 instances. On-Demand instances are not the most cost-effective option for the predictable off-peak traffic.pFor more information about Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/ec2ricing/reserved-instances/"Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pMigrate the website to AWS Elastic Beanstalk and Amazon EC2 R4 instances. Determine the minimum number of website instances required during off-peak times and use Reserved Instances to cover them while using On-Demand Instances to cover peak demand. Use Spot Fleet for the video analysis application comprised of R4 and Amazon EC2 R5 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. R4 instances are memory optimized and are not as cost-effective for web servers as T2 instances. Additionally, the memory-focused R family is not the best use case for compute-intensive video analysis.

question_content: pA company is migrating its marketing website and content management system from an on-premises data center to AWS. The company wants the AWS application to be deployed in a VPC with Amazon EC2 instances used for the web servers and an Amazon RDS instance for the database.pThe company has a runbook document that describes the installation process of the on-premises system. The company would like to base the AWS system on the processes referenced in the runbook document. The runbook document describes the installation and configuration of the operating systems, network settings, the website, and content management system software on the servers. After the migration is complete, the company wants to be able to make changes quickly to take advantage of other AWS features.pHow can the application and environment be deployed and automated in AWS with the LEAST operational overhead, while allowing for future changes?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the runbook to describe how to create the VPC, the EC2 instances, and the RDS instance for the application by using the AWS Console. Make sure that the rest of the steps in the runbook are updated to reflect any changes that may come from the AWS migration.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution does not include significant automation. It would be difficult to change the environment to use other services if necessary.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWrite a Python script that uses the AWS API to create the VPC, the EC2 instances, and the RDS instance for the application. Write shell scripts that implement the rest of the steps in the runbook. Have the Python script copy and run the shell scripts on the newly created instances to complete the installation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution includes some automation, but a Python script is not the best choice. Significant effort would be necessary to build the script. A Python script will require more operational overhead to handle future updates to the environment than a CloudFormation template will.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWrite an AWS CloudFormation template that creates the VPC, the EC2 instances, and the RDS instance for the application. Ensure that the rest of the steps in the runbook are updated to reflect any changes that may come from the AWS migration.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The CloudFormation template will help you build an automated solution. However, the installation and configuration of the software is still manual.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWrite an AWS CloudFormation template that creates the VPC, the EC2 instances, and the RDS instance for the application. Include EC2 user data in the AWS CloudFormation template to install and configure the software.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CloudFormation and Amazon EC2 user data scripts are the best option. You can use stack updates to deploy multiple versions of the template to change the environment in the future. pFor more information about CloudFormation, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-updating-stacks.html"AWS CloudFormation Stack Updates/a.

question_content: pA company stores many static files on premises. Users add a small number of new files each day. The company is refactoring and migrating some of its existing applications to AWS. The company expects this process to take 6 months. After the company completes the migration, each application will access the files directly from Amazon S3. During the migration, the files must remain accessible to the applications that the company is still running on premises. The on-premises applications run on multiple servers. The company does not want to maintain multiple copies of the static files.pHow should the company manage the daily migration and the on-premises access to the files?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway and connect the S3 File Gateway to the S3 bucket. Create an on-premises NFS file share for the existing on-premises directory to establish access to the files.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. S3 File Gateway supports a file interface with Amazon S3 and combines a service and a virtual software appliance. This combination can store and retrieve objects from Amazon S3 by using industry-standard file protocols, including NFS and SMB. NFS is a shared file system that can share data for multiple client connections. This solution will also provide access to the files for the on-premises applications.pFor more information about S3 File Gateway, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/StorageGatewayConcepts.html#file-gateway-concepts"Amazon S3 File Gateways/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS DataSync task to transfer the new files to the S3 bucket at the end of each day. Maintain the files on premises until the company completes the refactoring.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DataSync is an online data-transfer service that simplifies, automates, and accelerates the movement of data between on-premises storage systems and AWS storage services. DataSync would not provide access to the on-premises applications. The company would have to maintain a copy on premises. pFor more information about DataSync, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/what-is-datasync.html"What Is AWS DataSync?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway and connect the Volume Gateway to the S3 bucket. Create an on-premises iSCSI volume share for the existing on-premises directory to establish access to the files.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A Volume Gateway provides cloud-backed storage volumes that you can mount as iSCSI devices from on-premises application servers. However, you cannot connect multiple hosts to a Volume Gateway without additional configuration.pFor more information about how to use volumes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/GettingStarted-use-volumes.html"Using Your Volume/a. pFor more information about how to configure a Volume Gateway, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/create-volume-gateway-volume.html"Creating a Volume Gateway/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an S3 sync script and configure a recurring job to run the script at the end of each day. Maintain the files on premises until the company completes the refactoring and migration.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The S3 sync command synchronizes the contents of an S3 bucket and a local directory or the contents of two buckets. You could use this command to synchronize the data that is on premises to an S3 bucket. DataSync would not provide access to the on-premises applications. The company would have to maintain a copy on premises.pFor more information about the S3 sync command, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-services-s3-commands.html#using-s3-commands-managing-objects-sync"Sync Objects/a.

question_content: pA company wants to replace its call center system with a solution built using AWS managed services. The company call center would like the solution to receive calls, create contact flows, and scale to handle growth projections. The call center would also like the solution to use deep learning capabilities to recognize the intent of the callers and handle basic tasks, reducing the need to speak to an agent. The solution should also be able to query business applications and provide relevant information back to callers as requested.pWhich services should the solutions architect use to build this solution? (Select THREE.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon Rekognition to identify who is calling
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon Rekognition gives you the ability to add image and video analysis to your applications. This scenario is not an appropriate use case for Amazon Rekognition.pFor more information about Amazon Rekognition, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/rekognition/"Amazon Rekognition/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon Connect to create a cloud-based contact center
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You use Amazon Connect to create cloud-based contact centers, to design contact flows (similar to interactive voice response agents), and to onboard agents.pFor more information about Amazon Connect, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/category/amazon-connect/"Category: Amazon Connect/a. pFor more information about contact flows, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/userguide/contactflow.html"Create Amazon Connect Contact Flows/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon Alexa for Business to build conversational interfaces
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Alexa for Business provides features to control Alexa-compatible devices, enroll users, and assign skills at scale within an organization. This scenario is not an appropriate use case for Alexa for Business. pFor more information about Alexa, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/alexaforbusiness/#Benefits"Alexa for Business/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAWS Lambda to integrate with internal systems
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Amazon Lex uses AWS Lambda functions to query business applications, provide information back to callers, and make updates to information as needed.pFor more information about Lambda integration with Amazon Lex, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/lex/#Call_Center_Bots"Amazon Lex/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon Lex to recognize the intent of the caller
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use Amazon Lex to build conversational interfaces that use voice and text into any application. Amazon Lex provides the advanced deep learning functionalities of automatic speech recognition (ASR) to convert speech to text. Amazon Lex also provides natural language understanding (NLU) functionality to recognize conversational intent.pFor more information about Amazon Lex, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/lex/"Amazon Lex/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon SQS to add incoming callers to a queue
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon SQS gives users the ability to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. Amazon Connect manages a customer queue flow. You use Amazon SQS to send, store, and receive messages between software components. This scenario is not an appropriate use case for Amazon SQS. pFor more information about Amazon SQS, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/sqs/"Amazon SQS/a.

question_content: pA company has multiple AWS accounts with resources in different AWS Regions. The company uses a combination of security services, such as Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Macie, and AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Access Analyzer. A security team needs to provide regular audit reports on security findings and remediation efforts. The security team needs to see consolidated findings for all accounts.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an organization in AWS Organizations and activate AWS Security Hub in the management account. Designate a Security Hub administrator account and add the other AWS accounts as member accounts in Security Hub. Use the administrator account to report on the consolidated findings.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Organizations gives you the ability to create new AWS accounts programmatically. Security Hub provides a comprehensive view of your security state on AWS and evaluates environments according to security industry standards and best practices. When Organizations is activated, Security Hub can automatically detect new accounts that the company adds to the organization. This is the solution with the least operational overhead.pFor more information about Security Hub, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/what-is-securityhub.html"What Is AWS Security Hub?/a pFor more information about Organizations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-prereq-orgs.html"Using AWS Organizations to Manage Accounts/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pActivate AWS Security Hub in each AWS account. Designate an administrator account and add the other AWS accounts as member accounts. Create an aggregation Region in the administrator account. Use the aggregation Region in the administrator account to report on the consolidated findings.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Security Hub provides a comprehensive view of your security state on AWS and evaluates environments according to security industry standards and best practices. However, without Organizations, you would have to manually configure Security Hub in each new account. This solution would require unnecessary operational overhead. pFor more information about Security Hub, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/what-is-securityhub.html"What Is AWS Security Hub?/a pFor more information about Organizations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-prereq-orgs.html"Using AWS Organizations to Manage Accounts/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an organization in AWS Organizations and add all the accounts to the organization. Designate an AWS Audit Manager administrator account in the organization. Activate Audit Manager in the management account. Use the administrator account to run assessments and to view assessment reports.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Audit Manager continuously audits your AWS usage to assess risks and compliance with regulations and industry standards. However, you need Security Hub to consolidate findings from various AWS security services.pFor more information on Audit Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/audit-manager/latest/userguide/what-is.html"What Is AWS Audit Manager?/a pFor more information about Security Hub, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/what-is-securityhub.html"What Is AWS Security Hub?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pActivate AWS Audit Manager in each Region in each account where AWS resources are running. Create a custom framework that includes the controls and control sets. Share the custom framework with the other accounts. Run assessments and view assessments by using the framework.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Audit Manager continuously audits your AWS usage to assess risks and compliance with regulations and industry standards. However, you need Security Hub to consolidate findings from various AWS security services.pFor more information on Audit Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/audit-manager/latest/userguide/what-is.html"What Is AWS Audit Manager?/a pFor more information about Security Hub, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/what-is-securityhub.html"What Is AWS Security Hub?/a

question_content: pA company currently hosts a popular gaming application with an associated on-premises Redis database. The database stores player and leaderboard data. The company wants to migrate both the application and the Redis database to the AWS Cloud. The company will migrate the application to run on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The company requires the new database to be durable and to serve traffic with microsecond read latency. The company does not want to manage the database servers after the migration.pWhich solution will meet these requirements and store the data in the MOST durable way?

answer_choices.choice_content: pMigrate the on-premises application and the database to separate fleets of EC2 instances by using AWS Application Migration Service. Turn on Redis replication with replicas in different Availability Zones.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Significant server management effort would be necessary to run the database on EC2 instances. The company does not want to manage the database servers.pFor more information about managed databases on AWS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/frameworkerf-db.html"Database/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy an Amazon MemoryDB for Redis cluster to host the database. Configure at least one read replica for the MemoryDB cluster with Multi-AZ activated. Migrate the on-premises application servers by using AWS Application Migration Service. Take a snapshot of the existing Redis cluster and upload it to an Amazon S3 bucket. Seed the MemoryDB cluster with the Redis backup data.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Application Migration Service helps make the migration of on-premises servers to EC2 instances seamless. MemoryDB for Redis is a durable, in-memory managed database for workloads that require an ultra-fast, primary database. MemoryDB stores successful write operations durably in a distributed Multi-AZ transaction log. You can seed a MemoryDB cluster with a snapshot from an existing Redis cluster. You could access the existing snapshot by uploading the snapshot to an S3 bucket.pFor more information about Application Migration Service, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/what-is-application-migration-service.html"What Is AWS Application Migration Service?/a pFor more information about MemoryDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/what-is-memorydb-for-redis.html"What Is MemoryDB for Redis?/a pFor more information about durability and consistency in MemoryDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/consistency.html"Consistency/a. pFor more information about how to seed MemoryDB with a Redis snapshot, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/snapshots-seeding-redis.html"Seeding a New Cluster with an Externally Created Snapshot/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to host the database. Configure a Redis replication group with Multi-AZ activated. Migrate the on-premises application servers by using AWS Application Migration Service. Take a snapshot of the existing Redis cluster and upload it to an Amazon S3 bucket. Seed the ElastiCache cluster with the Redis backup data.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Although ElastiCache for Redis does support Multi-AZ deployment and has backup and recovery features, this service is not the most durable option to store Redis data on AWS because of the potential for data loss. Amazon MemoryDB for Redis is better suited for a workload that requires a durable database that provides ultra-fast performance.pFor more information about resilience in ElastiCache for Redis, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html"Resilience in Amazon ElastiCache/a. pFor more information about how to choose between MemoryDB and ElastiCache, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/related-services-choose-between-memorydb-and-redis.html"Related Services/a. pFor more information about durability and consistency in MemoryDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/consistency.html"Consistency/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy an Amazon MemoryDB for Redis cluster to host the database. Configure at least one read replica for the MemoryDB cluster with Multi-AZ activated. Migrate both the on-premises application and the database by using AWS Application Migration Service.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Application Migration Service helps make the migration of on-premises servers to EC2 instances seamless. Although Application Migration Service can migrate the application to EC2 instances, this service does not support managed databases such as MemoryDB.pFor more information about Application Migration Service, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/what-is-application-migration-service.html"What Is AWS Application Migration Service?/a

question_content: pA company is launching a web-based application in multiple Regions around the world. The application consists of both static content that the company stores in a private Amazon S3 bucket and dynamic content that the company hosts in Amazon ECS containers behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company requires that the static and dynamic application content be accessible through Amazon CloudFront only. pWhich combination of steps should a solutions architect recommend to restrict direct content access to CloudFront? (Select THREE.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a web ACL in AWS WAF with a rule to validate the presence of a custom header and associate the web ACL with the ALB.
answer_choices.solution_content: p Correct. You can use AWS WAF to validate custom headers. You can associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB.pFor more information about how to add custom headers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/add-origin-custom-headers.html"Adding Custom Headers to Origin Requests/a.pFor more information about web ACLs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl.html"Web Access Control Lists (Web ACLs)/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a web ACL in AWS WAF with a rule to validate the presence of a custom header and associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudFront adds the custom header. A web ACL in front of the CloudFront distribution would block any through traffic.pFor more information about how to add custom headers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/add-origin-custom-headers.html"Adding Custom Headers to Origin Requests/a.pFor more information about web ACLs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl.html"Web Access Control Lists (Web ACLs)/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure CloudFront to add a custom header to origin requests.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CloudFront can add a custom header to a request.pFor more information about how to add customer headers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/add-origin-custom-headers.html"Adding Custom Headers to Origin Requests/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the ALB to add a custom header to HTTP requests.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. ALBs have HTTP(S) listeners. ALBs do not create new headers.pFor more information about ALBs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html"What Is an Application Load Balancer?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the S3 bucket ACL to allow access from the CloudFront distribution only.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon S3 ACLs define which AWS accounts or groups have access.pFor more information about Amazon S3 ACLs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/acl-overview.html"Access Control List (ACL) Overview/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) and add it to the CloudFront distribution. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access to the OAC only.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use an OAC to restrict access to an S3 bucket to viewers who make requests through CloudFront.pFor more information about CloudFront OACs and Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuiderivate-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html"Restricting Access to an Amazon S3 Origin/a.

question_content: pA company has an online event-booking system that consists of a web application that is deployed in a five-instance fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances run Amazon Linux 2 with identical unencrypted root volumes. A solutions architect has created an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing configuration.pSometimes there is a gap of up to a month from when one event-booking window ends to when the next booking window begins. The company wants to shut off resources between event-booking windows. Currently, an administrator stops the instances after each event. However, the boot process is slow, and the long boot time is unacceptable when the company suddenly notifies the administrator that the next event-booking window is open. The company needs to find a solution that will stop and start the system quickly.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an encrypted snapshot of a root volume. Create a new AMI from the encrypted snapshot. Terminate the existing instances. Launch new instances by using the new AMI with hibernation turned on. Hibernate the instances when they are not in use.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A solution that hibernates instances will have the same cost implications as a solution that stops instances. It can be faster to restart hibernated instances than to restart stopped instances that take a long time to bootstrap. To use hibernation for supported EC2 instance types, you must configure hibernation when you first launch the EC2 instance. You can provide the required root volume encryption by creating an AMI from an encrypted snapshot of the existing volume. This solution would properly configure hibernation.pFor more information about EC2 instance hibernation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Hibernate.html"Hibernate Your On-Demand or Reserved Linux Instance/a. pFor more information about requirements for hibernation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/enabling-hibernation.html"Enable Hibernation for an Instance/a. pFor more information about how to encrypt root volumes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSEncryption.html"Encrypt Unencrypted Resources/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an encrypted snapshot of a root volume. Create a new root volume from the snapshot and attach it to the EC2 instances. Modify the EC2 instance options to turn on hibernation. Hibernate the instances when they are not in use.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A solution that hibernates instances will have the same cost implications as a solution that stops instances. It can be faster to restart hibernated instances than to restart stopped instances that take a long time to bootstrap. However, to use hibernation for supported EC2 instance types, you must configure hibernation when you first launch the EC2 instance.pFor more information about EC2 hibernation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Hibernate.html"Hibernate Your On-Demand or Reserved Linux Instance/a. pFor more information about requirements for hibernation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/enabling-hibernation.html"Enable Hibernation for an Instance/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a launch template by using the existing AMI. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group that uses the new launch template. Configure the minimum and desired number of instances to zero. Configure the maximum number of instances to five. Terminate the existing instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum of zero would terminate all instances that are running if they are not in use. This solution would require the instances to start fresh the for the next event-booking window. This solution would not reduce the boot time for newly launched instances.pFor more information about EC2 Auto Scaling, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/AutoScalingGroup.html"Auto Scaling Groups/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a launch template by using the existing AMI. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group that uses the new launch template. Configure the minimum and desired number of instances to one. Configure the maximum number of instances to five. Terminate the existing instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum of one would leave one instance running even if the instance is not in use. The company wants to turn off all instances between booking windows. Additionally, this solution would not reduce the boot time for newly launched instances.pFor more information about EC2 Auto Scaling, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/AutoScalingGroup.html"Auto Scaling Groups/a.

question_content: pA company wants to provide desktop as a service (DaaS) to a number of employees using Amazon WorkSpaces. WorkSpaces will need to access files and services hosted on premises with authorization based on the company's Active Directory. Network connectivity will be provided through an existing AWS Direct Connect connection.pThe solution has the following requirements:ul  liCredentials from Active Directory should be used to access on-premises files and services./li  liCredentials from Active Directory should not be stored outside the company./li  liEnd users should have single sign-on (SSO) to on-premises files and services once connected to WorkSpaces./li/ulpWhich strategy should the solutions architect use for end user authentication?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) directory within the WorkSpaces VPC. Use the Active Directory Migration Tool (ADMT) with the Password Export Server to copy users from the on-premises Active Directory to AWS Managed Microsoft AD. Set up a one-way trust allowing users from AWS Managed Microsoft AD to access resources in the on-premises Active Directory. Use AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the directory for WorkSpaces.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution copies the users to AWS Managed Microsoft AD. However, the company requires a solution that does not store credentials from Active Directory outside the company.pFor more information about AWS Managed Microsoft AD, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_microsoft_ad.html"AWS Managed Microsoft AD/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a service account in the on-premises Active Directory with the required permissions. Create an AD Connector in AWS Directory Service to be deployed on premises using the service account to communicate with the on-premises Active Directory. Ensure the required TCP ports are open from the WorkSpaces VPC to the on-premises AD Connector. Use the AD Connector as the directory for WorkSpaces.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot deploy AD Connector on premises.pFor more information about the requirements for AD Connector, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guiderereq_connector.html"AD Connector Prerequisites/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a service account in the on-premises Active Directory with the required permissions. Create an AD Connector in AWS Directory Service within the WorkSpaces VPC using the service account to communicate with the on-premises Active Directory. Use the AD Connector as the directory for WorkSpaces.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AD Connector is a directory gateway that you can use to redirect directory requests to your on-premises Active Directory without the need to cache any information in the cloud. This solution will authenticate the Active Directory credentials of the end users. The WorkSpaces will be members of the Active Directory that provide SSO to on-premises resources.pFor more information about AD Connector, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_ad_connector.html"Active Directory Connector/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) directory in the AWS Directory Service within the WorkSpaces VPC. Set up a one-way trust allowing users from the on-premises Active Directory to access resources in the AWS Managed Microsoft AD. Use AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the directory for WorkSpaces. Create an identity provider with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) from an on-premises ADFS server. Allow users from this identity provider to assume a role with a policy allowing them to run WorkSpaces.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. To set up AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) with Amazon WorkSpaces Web, you would also need to set up AWS Organizations.pFor more information about how to set up IAM Identity Center for WorkSpaces, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces-web/latest/adminguide/sso-idp.html"Set Up IAM Identity Center as Your IdP/a.

question_content: pA company plans to deploy a web application that will serve a global audience. The company will deploy the application by using Amazon EC2 instances across two AWS Regions. The company will create an Amazon Aurora global database, with a primary Aurora DB cluster in the first Region and a secondary Aurora DB cluster in the second Region. The company needs to minimize latency and ensure read-after-write consistency for the application’s database operations. The company also wants to regularly test its disaster recovery (DR) procedures to minimize data loss and maximize recovery speed across the two Regions.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the secondary Aurora DB cluster endpoint to perform read and write operations. Configure write forwarding to forward write operations to the primary Aurora DB cluster endpoint. Test the DR procedure by using managed planned failover.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An Aurora global database replicates data with minimal replication lag to a secondary Aurora DB cluster in another Region. This process optimizes read operations for the company's global audience. Write forwarding will allow the secondary DB cluster to accept write operations and will forward write operations to the primary DB cluster. Aurora handles networking across Regions. Aurora also provides multiple consistency modes for the strongest read-after-write consistency, including global consistency. Finally, managed planned failover automatically handles demotion, promotion, and all synchronization across the clusters with no data loss and faster recovery.pFor more information about write forwarding in an Aurora global database, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-write-forwarding.html"Using Write Forwarding in an Amazon Aurora Global Database/a. pFor more information about planned failover, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.html#aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.managed-failover"Using failover in an Amazon Aurora Global Database/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the secondary Aurora DB cluster endpoint to perform read operations. Use the primary Aurora DB cluster endpoint to perform write operations. Test the DR procedure by using managed planned failover.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An Aurora global database replicates data with minimal replication lag to a secondary Aurora DB cluster in another Region. This process optimizes read operations for the company's global audience. However, these read operations could provide stale information. This process will not achieve the required read-after-write consistency.pFor more information about Aurora global databases, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html"Using Amazon Aurora Global Databases/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the secondary Aurora DB cluster endpoint to perform read operations. Use the primary Aurora DB cluster endpoint to perform write operations. Test the DR procedure by using manual unplanned failover.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An Aurora global database replicates data with minimal replication lag to a secondary Aurora DB cluster in another Region. This process optimizes read operations for the company's global audience. However, these read operations could provide stale information. This process will not achieve the required read-after-write consistency.pFor more information about Aurora global databases, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html"Using Amazon Aurora Global Databases/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the secondary Aurora DB cluster endpoint to perform read and write operations. Configure write forwarding to forward write operations to the primary Aurora DB cluster endpoint. Test the DR procedure by using manual unplanned failover.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A manual unplanned failover process requires the manual performance of a series of tasks. You must detach and promote a secondary DB cluster. These steps are not suitable for the company's plan to test on a regular and frequent basis. A better solution would use managed planned failover, which would eliminate the manual steps and require less operational overhead.pFor more information about recovery from unplanned outages, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.html#aurora-global-database-failover"Recovering an Amazon Aurora Global Database from an Unplanned Outage/a.

question_content: pA company that designs multiplayer online games wants to expand its user base outside of Europe. The company transfers a significant amount of UDP traffic to keep all the live and interactive sessions of the games. The company has plans for rapid expansion and wants to build its architecture to provide an optimized online experience to its users.pWhich architecture will meet these requirements with the LOWEST latency for users?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up a Multi-AZ environment in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to cache user sessions.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudFront delivers HTML, CSS, JS, and image files, not UDP traffic.pFor more information about CloudFront, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html"What Is Amazon CloudFront?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up environments in multiple AWS Regions. Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator, and add endpoints from different Regions to it.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can reduce latency by setting up the access perimeter in multiple Regions. Global Accelerator is well suited for UDP (and gaming) services, among other use cases.pFor more information about Global Accelerator, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/faqs/"AWS Global Accelerator FAQs/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up environments in multiple AWS Regions. Use Amazon Route 53, and select latency-based routing.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Latency-based routing will route over the public internet instead of AWS's global network. Latency-based routing will not provide the same level of performance as Global Accelerator.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up a Multi-AZ environment in a single AWS Region. Use AWS Lambda@Edge to update sessions closer to the users.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In this solution, all customers will interact with a single Region. This solution can add to latency or performance issues.

question_content: pA company is designing a new application that stores data in Amazon S3. The company creates an S3 bucket with default settings. According to company regulations, no user can delete objects or write over objects in the S3 bucket for a minimum of 5 years after the initial storage of the objects.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock turned on. Configure Object Lock with a retention period of 5 years. Set the Object Lock retention to compliance mode. Move the existing objects to the new S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Object Lock with a 5-year retention period would lock the objects and prevent the objects from being overwritten or deleted. In compliance mode, objects cannot be overwritten or deleted by any user, including the root user of the account, for the duration of the retention period. Because you can configure Object Lock only when you first create a bucket, you would need a new bucket.pFor more information about Object Lock, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-overview.html"How S3 Object Lock Works/a. pFor more information about Object Lock retention modes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-overview.html#object-lock-retention-modes"Retention Modes/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the existing S3 bucket by turning on S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock. Configure Object Lock with a retention period of 5 years. Set the Object Lock retention to compliance mode.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can configure S3 Versioning for an existing S3 bucket, but you can configure Object Lock only when you first create a bucket. You cannot configure Object Lock for a bucket that already exists.pFor more information about Object Lock, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-overview.html"How S3 Object Lock Works/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the existing S3 bucket by turning on S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock. Configure Object Lock with a retention period of 5 years. Set the Object Lock retention to governance mode.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can configure S3 Versioning for an existing S3 bucket, but you can configure Object Lock only when you first create a bucket. You cannot configure Object Lock for a bucket that already exists. In governance mode, a user that has appropriate permissions could remove the lock and delete the objects.pFor more information about Object Lock, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-overview.html"How S3 Object Lock Works/a. pFor more information about Object Lock retention modes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-overview.html#object-lock-retention-modes"Retention Modes/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock turned on. Configure Object Lock with a retention period of 5 years. Set the Object Lock retention to governance mode. Move the existing objects to the new S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Object Lock with a 5-year retention period would lock the objects and prevent the objects from being overwritten or deleted. However, in governance mode, a user that has appropriate permissions could remove the lock and delete the objects.pFor more information about Object Lock, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-overview.html"How S3 Object Lock Works/a. pFor more information about Object Lock retention modes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-overview.html#object-lock-retention-modes"Retention Modes/a.

question_content: pA company recently deployed a new application that runs on a group of Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC. In a peered VPC, the company launched an EC2 Linux instance that serves as a bastion host. The security group of the application instances allows access only on TCP port 22 from the private IP of the bastion host. The security group of the bastion host allows access to TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 so that system administrators can use SSH to remotely log in to the application instances from several branch offices.pWhile looking through operating system logs on the bastion host, a cloud engineer notices thousands of failed SSH logins to the bastion host from locations around the world. The cloud engineer wants to change how remote access is granted to the application instances and wants to meet the following requirements:ul  liEliminate brute-force SSH login attempts./li  liRetain a log of commands run during an SSH session./li  liRetain the ability to forward ports./li/ulpWhich solution meets these requirements for remote access to the application instances?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the application instances to communicate with AWS Systems Manager. Grant access to the system administrators to use Session Manager to establish a session with the application instances. Terminate the bastion host.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Session Manager helps you improve your security posture by giving you the ability to close inbound SSH ports. With Session Manager, you do not need to manage SSH keys and certificates, bastion hosts, or jump boxes. Session Manager offers the benefit of port forwarding. Session Manager also logs and audits session activity.pFor more information about Session Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html"AWS Systems Manager Session Manager/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the security group of the bastion host to allow traffic from only the public IP addresses of the branch offices.
answer_choices.solution_content: pa target="_blank" href="http://"http:///a  pIncorrect.
