You would have to inspect the code of each application for usage of the old S3 bucket names, update the code, and test the code.pFor more information about Macie, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html"What is Amazon Macie?/a pFor more information about S3 encryption, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"Encrypting Existing Objects.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRun an Amazon Inspector report against the S3 bucket to identify sensitive data. Modify the S3 bucket to enable default encryption. Use an Amazon S3 Inventory report and Amazon S3 Batch Operations to encrypt the existing unencrypted objects in the same S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon Inspector is an automated service that continually scans AWS workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. However, Amazon Inspector does not examine S3 buckets for sensitive data.pFor more information about Amazon Inspector, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"What is Amazon Inspector?

answer_choices.choice_content: pRun an Amazon Macie report on the S3 bucket to identify sensitive data. Modify the S3 bucket to enable default encryption. Use an S3 Inventory report and S3 Batch Operations to encrypt the existing unencrypted objects in the same S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Macie is a service that can identify sensitive data in Amazon S3. You can use an S3 Inventory report to create a list of objects that need to be encrypted. You can use that list as the manifest for S3 Batch Operations to encrypt existing data. No code changes are necessary for the applications that access the S3 objects.pFor more information about Macie, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"What is Amazon Macie? pFor more information about S3 encryption, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"Encrypting Existing Objects.

question_content: pA company runs a three-tier architecture on AWS. The web tier and application tier run in Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups with a database as the backend. Scaling is based on CPU utilization of the application tier. The company creates an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue to decouple the web tier and the application tier. However, tests reveal that duplicate transactions occur and that the EC2 instances are not scaling. The lack of scaling sometimes delays application processing. A solutions architect needs to eliminate the duplicate transactions and correct the scaling delay.pWhich solution will meet these requirements in the MOST scalable way?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an SQS FIFO queue. Configure content-based deduplication. Update the application to use the new queue. Create an Amazon CloudWatch custom metric to calculate the backlog per instance that is acceptable to the company. Use a target tracking scaling policy based on the custom metric.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. FIFO queues can enhance message transmission between applications when the order of operations and events is critical or when duplicates are not acceptable. A custom metric to scale based on an acceptable backlog per instance would base the scaling on the system load in the SQS queue. The custom metric is calculated based on the approximate number of messages, processing latency, and the number of running EC2 instances. This solution provides more accurate scaling.pFor more information about scaling in response to activity in SQS queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html"Scaling Based on Amazon SQS/a. pFor more information about FIFO queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues.html"Amazon SQS FIFO (First-In-First-Out) Queues/a. pFor more information about high throughput for FIFO queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/high-throughput-fifo.html"High Throughput for FIFO Queues/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an SQS FIFO queue. Configure content-based deduplication. Update the application to use the new queue. Change the application tier scaling to use the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. FIFO queues can enhance message transmission between applications when the order of operations and events is critical or when duplicates are not acceptable. However, the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric will not change in proportion to the size of the Auto Scaling group that processes messages. A better solution is to use a custom metric based on an acceptable backlog per instance. A custom metric would scale better as the Auto Scaling group grows.pFor more information about scaling in response to activity in SQS queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html"Scaling Based on Amazon SQS/a. pFor more information about FIFO queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues.html"Amazon SQS FIFO (First-In-First-Out) Queues/a. pFor more information about high throughput for FIFO queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/high-throughput-fifo.html"High Throughput for FIFO Queues/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pChange the existing SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue. Configure content-based deduplication for the queue. Change the application tier scaling to use the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. FIFO queues can enhance message transmission between applications when the order of operations and events is critical or when duplicates are not acceptable. However, you cannot change an SQS standard queue to a FIFO queue.pFor more information about FIFO queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues.html"Amazon SQS FIFO (First-In-First-Out) Queues/a. pFor more information about how to configure a FIFO queue, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-moving.html"Moving from a Standard Queue to a FIFO Queue/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pChange the existing SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue. Configure content-based deduplication for the queue. Create an Amazon CloudWatch custom metric to calculate the backlog per instance that is acceptable to the company. Use a target tracking scaling policy based on the custom metric.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. FIFO queues can enhance message transmission between applications when the order of operations and events is critical or when duplicates are not acceptable. However, you cannot change an SQS standard queue to a FIFO queue.pFor more information about FIFO queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues.html"Amazon SQS FIFO (First-In-First-Out) Queues/a. pFor more information about how to configure a FIFO queue, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-moving.html"Moving from a Standard Queue to a FIFO Queue/a.

question_content: pA company deploys a new application on AWS. The application runs on two Amazon EC2 instances in two different Availability Zones behind an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application accesses an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.pWithin the first week, customers report that the application is having performance issues. Investigations identify two potential reasons for the performance issues: slow read responses from the RDS database and periodic high CPU utilization on the two EC2 instances. A solutions architect needs to implement changes to improve performance and to improve repetitive read responses for the new infrastructure. The solution must be fault-tolerant and must support native automated failover across Availability Zones.pWhich combination of configuration changes will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the instance size of the EC2 instances to meet CPU capacity requirements.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A change in the instance size could address the issues with high CPU utilization. However, without an Auto Scaling group to automatically replace failed instances, this solution would only partially meet the requirement for fault tolerance.pFor more information about how to change an EC2 instance size, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-resize.html"Change the Instance Type/a.pFor more information about Auto Scaling groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/AutoScalingGroup.html"Auto Scaling Groups/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd two more EC2 instances to host the application. Register the instances with the ALB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The addition of EC2 instances could address the CPU utilization issue. However, more than two additional instances might be necessary. Additionally, this solution would not meet the requirement for high availability because there is no automatic Multi-AZ failover response. An Auto Scaling group would be a better solution for scaling and high availability.pFor more information about Auto Scaling groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/AutoScalingGroup.html"Auto Scaling Groups/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across Availability Zones. Configure the EC2 Auto Scaling group to be the target for the ALB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An Auto Scaling group would give the application the ability to scale out when CPU utilization increases. A solution that spreads the EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones meets the requirement for high availability.pFor more information about Auto Scaling groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/AutoScalingGroup.html"Auto Scaling Groups/a.pFor more information about how to attach an ALB to an Auto Scaling group, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/attach-load-balancer-asg.html"Attaching a Load Balancer to Your Auto Scaling Group/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to cache responses from the RDS database.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. ElastiCache gives you the ability to set up, manage, and scale a distributed in-memory data store or cache environment in the cloud. However, ElastiCache for Memcached does not natively support automatic Multi-AZ failover. ElastiCache for Redis does meet this requirement.pFor more information about ElastiCache for Memcached, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/WhatIs.html"What Is Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached?/apFor more information about the differences between ElastiCache for Memcached and ElastiCache for Redis, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/SelectEngine.html"Comparing Memcached and Redis/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to cache responses from the RDS database.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. ElastiCache gives you the ability to set up, manage, and scale a distributed in-memory data store or cache environment in the cloud. An ElastiCache cluster to cache the RDS database responses can improve repetitive read response times. ElastiCache for Redis natively supports automatic Multi-AZ failover.pFor more information about ElastiCache for Redis, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/WhatIs.html"What Is Amazon ElastiCache for Redis?/a

question_content: pA company wants to move many different database engines on physical servers to AWS. Many of the databases use functionality that Amazon RDS does not currently support. The company wants to quickly rehost the database servers in the AWS Cloud.pWhich migration solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST migration effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Application Discovery Service to migrate the servers to new Amazon EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Application Discovery Service collects usage and configuration data about on-premises servers to help you plan migrations to the AWS Cloud. Application Discovery Service does not actually perform migrations.pFor more information about Application Discovery Service, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/what-is-appdiscovery.html"What Is AWS Application Discovery Service?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate new Amazon EC2 instances to host the databases. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the databases to AWS.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You would need to take multiple steps to create EC2 instances and use AWS DMS for migration. Multiple AWS DMS replication instances would be required, in addition to endpoints and tasks for the various database engines. A better solution would be to perform the lift and shift in a single pass with an agent installation.pFor more information about AWS DMS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/Welcome.html"What is AWS Database Migration Service?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the servers to new Amazon EC2 instances. Use general launch settings.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Application Migration Service is a highly automated lift-and-shift (rehost) solution that simplifies and accelerates migration to AWS. Application Migration Service can launch appropriate EC2 instances that match the on-premises servers and any software that runs on those servers. question_content: pA solutions architect needs to create an infrastructure proposal for a web application. The application requires a resilient and highly available design across multiple Availability Zones. The solutions architect proposes the following:  ul    liA VPC with an internet gateway and a NAT gateway/li    liOne public subnet and one private subnet each in two different Availability Zones/li    liAn Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group spread across multiple Availability Zones behind an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB)/li    liAmazon DynamoDB tables to store data/li  /ul  What should the solutions architect do to increase the resilience and availability of the proposed architecture?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a second internet gateway. Attach each internet gateway to a different subnet.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You do not need to create a second internet gateway to achieve a resilient architecture across Availability Zones. By default, an internet gateway is a highly available and scalable component that is managed by AWS.pFor more information about internet gateways, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Internet_Gateway.html"Connect Subnets to the Internet Using an Internet Gateway/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a second internet-facing ALB. Attach each ALB to a different subnet.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You do not need to create a second internet-facing ALB to achieve a resilient architecture across Availability Zones. By default, an ALB is a highly available and scalable resource that is managed by AWS.pFor more information about ALBs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/application-load-balancers.html"Application Load Balancers/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a second NAT gateway. Update the route tables on each private subnet as needed.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You need to create a second NAT gateway in a separate Availability Zone to achieve a resilient architecture across Availability Zones. A NAT gateway is highly available only within the Availability Zone where it is deployed.pFor more information about the availability of NAT gateways, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html#nat-gateway-basics"NAT Gateway Basics/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate DynamoDB global tables with two replicated tables that are stored in different AWS Regions.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DynamoDB global tables are not necessary for this solution. Data in DynamoDB tables is automatically replicated across multiple Availability Zones in the Region where the tables are created. You do not need to create a global DynamoDB table to achieve a resilient architecture across Availability Zones.pFor more information about DynamoDB high availability, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html"What Is Amazon DynamoDB?/a

question_content: pA company has multiple on-premises data centers around the world. The company wants to migrate 150 VMs to AWS with minimal downtime. The company also needs to migrate 300 TB of data to a single AWS Region. With the company's current internet connection, the data migration would take 5 days.pWhich combination of tools and services will provide the FASTEST migration to AWS?

Incremental Application Migration Service replication minimizes the business impact that is associated with application downtime during the final cutover.pFor more information about S3 Transfer Acceleration, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/s3/transfer-acceleration"S3 Transfer Acceleration/a. pFor more information about migration tools and services, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/application-migration-service/faqs"AWS Application Migration Service FAQs/a.

question_content: pA company is planning to migrate a mix of Windows-based applications and Linux-based applications that run on on-premises physical servers to Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to manage and monitor the migration from the AWS Management Console by using Amazon CloudWatch and AWS CloudTrail. The company needs to control the migration process permissions and access by using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pInstall the AWS Replication Agent on each source server. Initialize AWS Application Migration Service. Configure the launch settings and deploy the target EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS Application Migration Service is a highly automated lift-and-shift solution that simplifies and accelerates the migration to AWS for applications that are running on physical servers and VMs. This solution can be managed and monitored from the console and can be used with IAM, CloudWatch, and CloudTrail.pFor more information about Application Migration Service, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/what-is-application-migration-service.html"What Is AWS Application Migration Service?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pInstall and register the VMware Hybrid Cloud Extension (HCX) connector. Select servers from the company's server catalog. Configure the replication settings and deploy the target EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. VMware HCX automates the migration of on-premises VMs to the AWS Cloud. VMware HCX can be used only for VMs, not the physical servers that the company intends to migrate.pFor more information about VMware HCX, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.comrescriptive-guidance/latestatterns/migrate-vmware-sddc-to-vmware-cloud-on-aws-using-vmware-hcx.html"Migrate VMware SDDC to VMware Cloud on AWS Using VMware HCX/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pInstall the AWS Discovery Agent on each source server. Turn on the data collection option in AWS Migration Hub. Start the agents to collect the data.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Application Discovery Service collects usage and configuration data about on-premises servers to help you plan migrations to the AWS Cloud by. Application Discovery Service requires additional services to perform the actual migration.pFor more information about Application Discovery Service, see ua target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/what-is-appdiscovery.html"What Is AWS Application Discovery Service?/a/u

answer_choices.choice_content: pInstall the AWS Systems Manager Agent on each source server. Create a blueprint for the target environment. Use AWS Systems Manager to migrate to EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Incorrect. AWS Systems Manager allows users to efficiently manage resources on AWS, in multicloud and hybrid environments. It is not used for migrating applications to AWS Cloud.pFor more information about AWS Systems Manager, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/what-is-systems-manager.html"What is AWS Systems Manager?/a

question_content: pA company has resources in on-premises networks and in multiple VPCs on AWS. The company needs a networking solution that will give the on-premises resources the ability to communicate with the VPC resources. The VPC resources also must be able to communicate with each other.pThe company has configured a customer gateway device on premises and has attached virtual private gateways to each VPC. The company wants a scalable solution so that the company can easily add more VPCs in the future.pHow should a solutions architect configure the network connectivity to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an individual AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the customer gateway device and each of the virtual private gateways. Configure VPC peering connections between all the VPCs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Site-to-Site VPN is a fully managed service that creates a secure connection between on-premises resources and AWS resources by using IPsec tunnels. A VPC peering connection is a network connection between two VPCs that gives you the ability to route traffic between the VPCs by using private addresses. A significant amount of operational overhead would result from the creation and management of multiple VPN connections and VPC peering connections.pFor more information about Site-to-Site VPN, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html"What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?/a pFor more information about how to peer VPCs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latesteering/what-is-vpc-peering.html"What is VPC Peering?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a transit gateway. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN attachment between the customer gateway device and the transit gateway. Attach the VPCs to the transit gateway. Remove the virtual private gateways.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A transit gateway is a network transit hub that you can use to interconnect VPCs and on-premises networks. All the necessary connections can occur through a single transit gateway, minimizing operational overhead.pFor more information about transit gateways, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html"What is a Transit Gateway?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up a connection through AWS Direct Connect. Create VIFs to provide access to the virtual private gateways. Configure VPC peering connections between all the VPCs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Direct Connect can connect on-premises networks to AWS. This solution would require the configuration and management of a Direct Connect connection and multiple VPC peering connections, significantly increasing operational overhead.pFor more information about Direct Connect, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html"What is AWS Direct Connect?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a transit VPC. Create VPN connections from the transit VPC to each virtual private gateway. Create AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections between the customer gateway device and the transit VPC.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A transit VPC is a common way to connect geographically dispersed VPCs and remote networks to create a global network transit center. However, a transit VPC requires additional configuration and operational overhead because you must manage Amazon EC2 instances. With a transit gateway, there are no EC2 instances to manage.pFor more information about transit VPCs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-scalable-secure-multi-vpc-network-infrastructure/transit-vpc-solution.html"Transit VPC Solution/a.

question_content: pA company has a serverless application that is backed by an Amazon RDS database. The company's AWS Lambda functions share the same user account to access the database.pA database administrator updates the password in the database to comply with security policies. Shortly after the update, several Lambda functions fail. The user receives an error message for credentials that are not valid. After investigating the error, a solutions architect discovers that the affected Lambda functions use hardcoded credentials. The solutions architect needs to address the errors and improve the security of the credentials.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore the user name and password in AWS Secrets Manager. Update the Lambda functions to retrieve the user name and password from Secrets Manager. Configure an alternating users automatic rotation of the credentials as required.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Secrets Manager replaces hardcoded credentials with API calls to retrieve secrets programmatically. You can configure Secrets Manager to automatically rotate RDS database passwords. An alternating users rotation updates credentials for two users in one secret. However, in this scenario, the database has only a single application user account.pFor more information about Secrets Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html"What is AWS Secrets Manager?/a pFor more information about rotation strategies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets_strategies.html"Rotation Strategies/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a Lambda function to update the credentials in the RDS database. Schedule the Lambda function to run as required. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes a Lambda function to update the hardcoded passwords whenever the password is changed in the RDS database.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Significant code development would be required to create multiple Lambda functions to rotate the passwords both in the database and the applications.pFor more information about EventBridge notifications for Amazon RDS, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"Creating a Rule that Triggers on an Amazon RDS Event.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore the user name and password in AWS Secrets Manager. Update the Lambda functions to retrieve the user name and password from Secrets Manager. Configure a single user automatic rotation of the credentials as required.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Secrets Manager replaces hardcoded credentials with API calls to retrieve secrets programmatically. You can configure Secrets Manager to automatically rotate RDS database passwords. In this scenario, the database has a single application user account. For this reason, the single user rotation strategy would be appropriate. This solution requires no new Lambda functions, so it requires the least development effort.pFor more information about Secrets Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html"What is AWS Secrets Manager?/a pFor more information about rotation strategies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets_strategies.html"Rotation Strategies/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Update the Lambda functions to retrieve the user name and password from Parameter Store. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes a Lambda function to update Parameter Store whenever the password is changed in the RDS database.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameter Store can securely store the credentials. However, the creation of an extra Lambda function to rotate the password involves significant code development. This solution also requires manual updates of the database.pFor more information about Parameter Store, se href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html" AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store/a.

question_content: pA company has created an Amazon CloudFront distribution with two Amazon S3 buckets as origins. The company discovers that objects in both S3 buckets are publicly accessible. The desired state for the first S3 bucket is to allow access through CloudFront and other AWS resources with appropriate permissions. Objects in the second S3 bucket should be accessible only through CloudFront for all users except for the S3 bucket owner.pHow should a solutions architect configure access to the buckets to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM policy and an IAM role that allow access to the first S3 bucket. Assign the role to the CloudFront distribution and the other resources that need access to the first S3 bucket. Create an origin access control (OAC) for the CloudFront distribution. Create an S3 bucket policy for the second S3 bucket that allows access only with the OAC as the principal.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can assign an IAM role to certain AWS resources. However, you cannot assign an IAM role to a CloudFront distribution.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a separate S3 bucket policy for each S3 bucket. Configure the policy for the first S3 bucket to allow read access to appropriate AWS resources and the CloudFront distribution as principals. Configure the policy for the second S3 bucket to allow only read access for the CloudFront distribution as the principal.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use an S3 bucket policy to restrict access to the objects. However, you cannot list a CloudFront distribution as a principal. An OAC must represent the CloudFront distribution for both bucket policies.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a separate origin access control (OAC) for the CloudFront distribution for each S3 bucket. Configure the first OAC to include access for the other AWS resources. Configure the second OAC to include only CloudFront. Update the S3 bucket policies to restrict access to the correct OACs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An OAC is a special CloudFront user that is associated with S3 origins to secure all or some of the S3 content. However, an OAC cannot include principal information from AWS resources other than CloudFront.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a separate origin access control (OAC) for the CloudFront distribution for each S3 bucket. Create an S3 bucket policy for the first S3 bucket that allows access to the appropriate AWS resources and the OAC as principals. Create an S3 bucket policy for the second S3 bucket that allows access to the appropriate OAC as the principal.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An OAC is a special CloudFront user that is associated with S3 origins to secure all or some S3 content. You can use an S3 bucket policy to restrict access to the objects. You can list an OAC as a principal in a resource policy.pFor more information about how to use an OAC to restrict access to S3 content, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuiderivate-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html"Restricting Access to an Amazon S3 Origin/a.pFor more information about resource-based policies, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_identity-vs-resource.html"Identity-Based Policies and Resource-Based Policies/a.

question_content: pA company wants to store thousands of objects in Amazon S3. Object key names can have the following prefixes:ul  limk (marketing)/li  lisa (sales)/li  liex (executive)/li/ulpAccess should be based on the following rules:ul  liMarketing managers must have access only to objects with the mk prefix./li  liSales managers must have access only to objects with the sa prefix./li  liSales and marketing directors must have access to objects with both the mk and sa prefixes./li  liThe finance administrator needs access to all objects with any prefix./li/ulpThe company needs an access solution that provides the ability to add more prefixes in the future.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST ongoing administrative effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate four S3 buckets. Separate the mk, sa, and ex objects into three separate S3 buckets. Replicate the mk and sa objects into the fourth S3 bucket and the ex S3 bucket. Define the appropriate IAM resource-based policy for each S3 bucket to control access. Give the correct URL for each S3 bucket to each employee.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would separate access and would provide a single URL for each employee. However, if you add a new prefix later, you would have to create a new S3 bucket and replicate the new bucket to the ex bucket. This solution does not require the least ongoing administrative effort.pFor more information about S3 replication, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html"Replicating Objects/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate one S3 bucket. Place all the objects in the S3 bucket. Create multiple appropriate IAM policies based on the three prefixes. Attach the correct IAM policy to each object in the S3 bucket based on the object name. Give the single URL for the S3 bucket to all employees.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A policy defines the permissions for the identities or resources with which the policy is associated. You cannot attach IAM policies directly to objects. You must attach IAM resource-based policies to the S3 buckets.pFor more information about IAM resource-based policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_resource-based"Resource-Based Policies/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate one S3 bucket. Create a folder with subfolders for the mk and sa objects. Attach the appropriate IAM resource-based policies to the folders. Create a separate folder for the ex objects. Define the appropriate IAM resource-based policy on the S3 bucket for the finance administrator. Give the folder URLs to the managers and directors. Give the S3 bucket URL to the finance administrator.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A policy defines the permissions for the identities or resources with which the policy is associated. You cannot attach IAM policies directly to folders in an S3 bucket. You must attach IAM resource-based policies to the S3 buckets.pFor more information about IAM resource-based policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_resource-based"Resource-Based Policies/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate one S3 bucket. Place all the objects in the S3 bucket. Create three S3 access points that are based on the object prefixes for mk, sa, and both. Attach the appropriate IAM resource-based policies to the S3 access points and the S3 bucket. Give the appropriate S3 access point aliases to the managers and directors. Give the URL for the S3 bucket to the finance administrator.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. S3 access points simplify data access for any AWS service or customer application that stores data in Amazon S3. You can attach IAM policies directly to the S3 access points. Employees would have a single URL to access their objects. This solution also gives the company a flexible way to add S3 access points for future prefixes.pFor more information about S3 access points, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-points.html"Managing Data Access with Amazon S3 Access Points/a. pFor more information about IAM resource-based policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_resource-based"Resource-Based Policies/a.

question_content: pA global company uses multiple accounts. Each account runs resources in three AWS Regions. The company needs identical Amazon EC2 instances as test systems in the different accounts. A solutions architect creates a custom AMI and an AWS CloudFormation template to provision the test systems in the company's main development account. The solutions architect shares the AMI across accounts and copies the AMI to each Region. The solutions architect shares the CloudFormation template to the various accounts and edits the template to refer to the appropriate AMI ID for each Region. The solutions architect needs to reduce the manual work that is necessary to create each new custom AMI.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameters that have identical names in each Region for each account. Include the appropriate AMI IDs for that Region in the parameters. Configure the CloudFormation template to retrieve the AMI ID from the parameters. Use the single CloudFormation template in the main development account to provision the test systems in all the accounts. Update the parameters as required when the company creates and shares a new AMI.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A CloudFormation template can create resources only in the account where the template resides. This solution would not give the solutions architect the ability to provision test systems in the other accounts.pFor more information about CloudFormation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html"What Is AWS CloudFormation?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameters that have identical names in each Region for each account. Include the appropriate AMI IDs for that Region. Configure the CloudFormation template to retrieve the AMI ID from the parameters. Copy the CloudFormation template to each account and Region. Use the template to create the required resources. Update the parameters as required when the company creates and shares a new AMI.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameter Store provides storage for configuration data, including passwords, database strings, and AMI IDs. Less operational overhead is required to store the AMI ID in Parameter Store than to hardcode the AMI IDs in the CloudFormation templates. A solution that relies on maintenance of parameters in each account and of multiple CloudFormation templates will require more operational overhead than a solution that uses CloudFormation StackSets and mappings.pFor more information about Parameter Store, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html"AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store/a. pFor more information about mappings, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/mappings-section-structure.html"Mappings/a. pFor more information about StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html"Working with AWS CloudFormation StackSets/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a mapping section in the CloudFormation template to hold the AMI IDs for each Region. Update the template to retrieve the correct AMI ID from the mapping. Import the CloudFormation template into each account. Use the template to create the required resources. Update the mapping as required when the company creates and shares a new AMI.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A solution that uses mappings in a CloudFormation template requires less operational overhead than a solution that hardcodes the AMI IDs. Maintenance of multiple CloudFormation templates would require more operational overhead than usage of CloudFormation StackSets.pFor more information about CloudFormation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html"What Is AWS CloudFormation?/a pFor more information about mappings, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/mappings-section-structure.html"Mappings/a. pFor more information about StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html"Working with AWS CloudFormation StackSets/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a mapping section in the CloudFormation template to hold the AMI IDs for each Region. Update the template to retrieve the correct AMI ID from the mapping. Use CloudFormation StackSets to create a stack set in the main development account. Use the stack set to deploy stack instances in each account as needed. Update the mapping as required when the company creates and shares a new AMI.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. StackSets extends the functionality of CloudFormation stacks by giving users tools to manage stacks across multiple accounts and Regions. A solution that uses mappings in a CloudFormation template and creates a single stack set to deploy multiple stack instances to the multiple accounts and Regions would require less operational overhead than a solution that requires maintenance of multiple CloudFormation templates.pFor more information about StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html"Working with AWS CloudFormation StackSets/a. pFor more information about mappings, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/mappings-section-structure.html"Mappings/a.

question_content: pA company uses AWS Organizations with all features turned on to manage multiple AWS accounts. The tag names and values that are applied to the resources across accounts are inconsistent. The company wants to generate cost allocation reports based on a standardized set of tag names and values. The company needs to identify and correct noncompliant tags. After these corrections, the company will enforce the use of the standardized tags.pHow can a solutions architect correct the noncompliant tags and enforce the use of only compliant tags in the future?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Config to create managed rules in each account. Use the required-tags rule to apply specific tags to the AWS resources. Activate AWS Config for the organization. Create a custom AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to automatically apply the appropriate tag to the AWS resource.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Config managed rules can detect and automatically correct noncompliant resources in AWS. However, you cannot use AWS Config to enforce the use of compliant tags in the future.pFor more information about AWS Config managed rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_use-managed-rules.html"AWS Config Managed Rules/a. pFor more information about the AWS Config required-tags rule, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/required-tags.html"Required-Tags/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate tag policies in Organizations for the required tags. Select the option to prevent noncompliant operations for this tag to enforce use of the tags. Attach the tag policies to the organization entities as required. Use AWS Resource Groups to find noncompliant tags. Correct the tags by using the AWS service that created the resources.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Tag policies help standardize tags across resources in an organization's accounts. You can use Resource Groups to detect noncompliant resources and generate a report so that you can make corrections. However, the option to prevent noncompliant operations for this tag would not have any effect on resources that are created with no tags. answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate tag policies in Organizations for the required tags. Attach the tag policies to the organization entities as required. Use AWS Resource Groups to find noncompliant tags. Correct the tags by using the AWS service that created the resources. Use SCPs to enforce the use of the tags across the organization.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Tag policies help standardize tags across resources in an organization's accounts. answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule to monitor the addition of noncompliant tags to an AWS resource. Configure the rule to send a message to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure the SQS queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function to apply an appropriate tag to the AWS resource.
